heading: Removing highly memorized examples hurts test accuracy more than random removal
definition: removing the training examples whose labels a network memorizes most (those whose inclusion most raises the chance of predicting their own label correctly) and retraining lowers test accuracy more than removing as many random examples (ResNet-50 on CIFAR-100 and ImageNet; Feldman & Zhang 2020). The effect is much smaller on MNIST.
summary: A separate study reports larger losses for partially fine-tuned DistilBERT, using a different method to estimate how strongly each example was memorized. Replication using the original estimation method and image settings remains unestablished.

suggested_status.by_scale: R2 for the removal comparison in the reported settings using a proxy ranking; parameter-scale status cannot be assigned because versions.V8.studies_by_size contains only 'not stated'. The exact inclusion-based estimator and original image/MNIST settings retain original-source evidence.
suggested_status.reason: arXiv:2203.12171 independently reports larger accuracy losses than random removal for partially fine-tuned DistilBERT and a feature-based MLP (R1–R5), extending the direction reported by arXiv:2008.03703 (R1–R3). counts: versions.V8.verdicts.supports.studies = 1 and versions.V8.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original = 0. The supporting extension changes the memorization estimator. arXiv:2307.10736#R1–R2 supplies no random-controlled replication.
suggested_status.open_questions: An independent experiment using the original inclusion-based estimator, end-to-end ResNet-50 on CIFAR-100 and ImageNet, and the MNIST comparison would establish whether R2 applies to those exact conditions. A failed matched replication or credible estimator-artifact result could change the status.

source.title: What Neural Networks Memorize and Why: Discovering the Long Tail via Influence Estimation

original_result.setup: Feldman and Zhang removed examples selected by estimated memorization and retrained ResNet50 on ImageNet and CIFAR-100 and simplified Inception on MNIST.
original_result.result: On ImageNet, removing approximately 32% of examples with memorization estimates ≥0.3 reduced accuracy by approximately 3.4 percentage points, versus approximately 2.6 for equally sized random removal. CIFAR-100 showed the same direction; the effect was much smaller on MNIST.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: Influence-ranked removal of equal numbers of examples hurt accuracy more than random removal across four datasets.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: Whether the random-controlled removal effect persists across parameter-scale buckets, particularly at 1–10B, 10–100B and above 100B.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V8.studies_by_size and versions.V8.coverage_by_operation.removal.by_size contain only 'not stated'; the pack supplies no controlled parameter-scaling comparison. Tested settings are documented in arXiv:2008.03703#R1–R3, arXiv:2203.12171#R1–R5 and arXiv:2307.10736#R1–R2.

wording_issues.phrase: those whose inclusion most raises the chance of predicting their own label correctly
wording_issues.issue: This specifies the original inclusion-based estimator. The independent supporting results rank examples using influence-function self-influence, so they establish the removal comparison under a proxy ranking rather than reproduce that estimator.

wording_issues.phrase: The effect is much smaller on MNIST.
wording_issues.issue: The corrected MNIST subject is simplified Inception, whereas the ImageNet and CIFAR-100 subjects are ResNet-50. The reported comparison changes architecture along with dataset.

method_sensitivity.what: The original reports a much smaller removal effect on MNIST with simplified Inception than on CIFAR-100 and ImageNet with ResNet-50. Its method-sensitivity summary associates the effect with dataset variability and number of examples; these rows do not isolate dataset from architecture.

After removing training examples selected through high-influence pairs on CIFAR-100, full-test accuracy changes from 76.06 ± 0.28% to 73.52 ± 0.25%; accuracy on the selected highly influenced test examples changes from 72.14 ± 1.32% to 45.38 ± 1.45%. Both comparisons use full-data training as their baseline and supply no random-removal control. They show accuracy losses under different evaluation conditions, but cannot determine V8's comparison with equal-sized random removal.

In the SST-2 Linear-versus-DNN experiment, high removal percentages also discard examples from main subpopulations, sharply worsening both classifiers. Their error gap becomes statistically non-significant. This concerns the gap between classifiers; without random removal it cannot establish or challenge V8's comparison.
